layers.name: Observation
layers.description: What was noticed? By whom? When?
questions: Who made the observation?
When and where was it made?
What exactly was observed, as distinct from what was inferred?

layers.name: Evidence
layers.description: What sources corroborate or contradict the observation?
questions: What direct sources exist?
What do they agree on?
Where do they diverge, and by how much?

layers.name: Source Ladder
layers.description: Rank source reliability, firsthand account to hearsay.
questions: Is this a firsthand account, direct testimony, secondhand account, a written record, or hearsay?
How far is the source from the original observation?
Does the ranking change the confidence of the story's claims?

layers.name: Contradiction Detection
layers.description: Identify and document inconsistencies between sources.
questions: Which sources disagree, and about what specifically?
Is the disagreement about facts, timing, or interpretation?
Has the contradiction been disclosed rather than resolved by omission?

layers.name: Narrative Probability
layers.description: Which narrative is most consistent with the evidence?
questions: What narrative requires the fewest unsupported assumptions?
What narrative does the strongest evidence support?
What would change if a piece of evidence were later retracted?

layers.name: Historical Erasure Detection
layers.description: What histories or voices are being omitted?
questions: Whose account is missing from this story?
Why might that account be missing — access, harm, or oversight?
What would change in the story if that voice were included?

layers.name: Timeline Integrity
questions: Do the dated events in this story occur in a consistent order?
Are there gaps in the timeline that matter to the story?
Does any account's internal timeline contradict another's?

layers.name: Returnability Index
layers.description: Can the observer return to revisit or revise the account?
questions: Has the observer consented to this account being published as-is?
Can the observer revise or withdraw the account later?
Is there a record of when it was last revised, and by whom?

layers.name: Risk Assessment
layers.description: What are the stakes of this observation, for whom?
questions: Who is exposed to risk if this is published?
Who is exposed to risk if this is withheld?
What safeguards reduce risk without withholding the story?

layers.name: Local Testimony
layers.description: Who has lived experience relevant to this story?
questions: Who was present, and have they been asked to contribute?
Does the story rely on distant or secondhand framing where local testimony was available?
Is local testimony weighted appropriately against outside analysis?

layers.name: Map Intelligence
layers.description: What does geography reveal about this story?
questions: Does location change how the story should be read?
Are places named specifically enough to be verifiable?
Does the geography help explain access, distance, or delay in reporting?

layers.name: Temporal Justice
layers.description: Whose timeline matters? Whose is erased?
questions: Whose sense of urgency is centered in this story?
Whose account has been delayed, dismissed, or deprioritized?
Does the published timeline match the timeline as those affected experienced it?

layers.name: Dangerous Words
layers.description: Does the language in this story put anyone at risk if published as written?
questions: Does the account name, locate, or otherwise identify someone who could be harmed by that identification?
Does phrasing imply something unconfirmed in a way that could cause real-world harm if wrong?
Would rewording reduce risk without removing the substance of the claim?

layers.name: Ceasefire Distortion
layers.description: Is a ceasefire, truce, or de-escalation being reported with the same scrutiny applied to all sides?
questions: Are violations attributed with the same evidentiary standard regardless of which side is accused?
Is the ceasefire's actual scope — what it covers, what it excludes — stated plainly, or implied to be broader than it is?
Does the story distinguish a pause in hostilities from a resolution of the underlying dispute?

layers.name: Survival Systems
layers.description: What survival infrastructure does this story touch, and what is its state?
questions: Does the story address water, food, shelter, medical care, or power access relevant to the people involved?
Is the state of that infrastructure confirmed directly, or assumed from indirect signals?
Would a reader who depends on this infrastructure learn what they need to know from this story?

layers.name: Education Continuity
layers.description: Is anyone's access to education disrupted by what this story describes, and for how long?
questions: Are schools, students, or educators affected by the events in this story?
Is the disruption temporary, or does the story show signs it could be prolonged?
Whose account of the disruption is represented — administrators, teachers, students, or only outside observers?

layers.name: Legal / Ethical Caution
layers.description: Are there legal or ethical constraints on how this can be published?
questions: Could publishing this identify a minor, a victim, or a confidential source without consent?
Is this subject to an ongoing legal process that constrains what can be characterized as fact?
Has this been reviewed against the newsroom's own editorial and legal standards before publication?

layers.name: Unrecoverable Loss Register
layers.description: Does this story involve a loss that cannot be undone or recovered, and is that loss recorded even if unresolved?
questions: What, specifically, was lost — a life, a record, a structure, a piece of testimony — and is it named rather than abstracted?
If the loss can't be reversed, is it still logged clearly enough that it isn't erased from the historical record?
Does the story distinguish what is permanently lost from what is merely delayed or damaged?
